newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi stocks plunge on petroleum, budget worries.
newsitem.headline: Delhi stocks plunge on petroleum, budget worries.

text.p: Delhi stocks plunged to close sharply lower on Monday on fears of an impending hike in petroleum product prices and worries over changes in the budgetary proposals for 1997/98 (April-March), brokers said.
The benchmark index closed 17.70 points lower at 772.84.

Foreign institutional investors (FIIs) and others sold sizeable amounts of shares throughout the session, and automobile stocks seen affected by petroleum price hikes were among the worst hit, they said.
Selective purchases by financial institutions failed to check the declining trend, they said.

Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral and Finance Minister P. Chidambaram expressed concern last week on Indian oil prices ruling below world levels, and Gujral said a bold decision on the issue was unvoidable.
Parliament is expected vote on the 1997/98 budget, which proposed tax cuts and import duty reductions, on Friday.
Communist partners in the ruling centre-left coalition are seeking amendments in the budget welcomed by industry, and have described some budgetary proposals as pro-rich.
"The CBI (Central Bureau of Investigation's) decision to prosecute Janata Dal president Laloo Prasad Yadav in the fodder scam also hit the sentiment," said Ashok Arya of brokers S.C. Gupta and Co.
Yadav, chief minister of the state of Bihar and head of Gujral's Janata Dal party, has denied any wrongdoing in the scandal involving diversion of animal welfare funds.
But his refusal to quit office and face trial in the case is seen as having hurt the image of his party.
Scooter-maker Bajaj Auto plunged 47.50 rupees, or about five percent, to 860.50 while truck-maker TELCO fell 11.20 rupees to 381.
Reliance fell 5.95 rupees to 298.55 while TISCO fell 8.40 rupees to 171.95.
State Bank of India lost 11.70 rupees at 301.25.
